references.text: God promises to provide bread from heaven for the people day by day—a foreshadowing of the daily provision of bread that Jesus asks for in the Lord's Prayer.
The manna God gave the Israelites in the wilderness is the background for the prayer for daily bread. The people received what they needed for each day.
Agur prays: 'Give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with the food that I need'—a parallel to the prayer for daily bread, neither more nor less than what one needs.
All creatures wait on God to receive their food in due time, and when He opens His hand, they are filled with good things—God as the daily provider.
The eyes of all look to You, Lord, and You give them their food in due time. You open Your hand and satisfy every living thing—expressing trust in God's daily care.

The parallel passage in Matthew's version of the Lord's Prayer: 'Give us today our daily bread' (τὸν ἄρτον ἡμῶν τὸν ἐπιούσιον δὸς ἡμῖν σήμερον). Luke uses 'each day' (τὸ καθʼ ἡμέραν) instead of 'today' (σήμερον).
Jesus urges the disciples not to worry about food and drink, for their heavenly Father knows what they need—the same trust in God's daily provision expressed in the prayer.
Paul assures that God will supply all their needs according to His riches in glory in Christ Jesus—God's daily provision for His children.
'If we have food and clothing, let us be content with these'—an attitude of satisfaction with daily bread, without craving more than what is necessary.

God humbled the people and let them hunger, then gave them manna to teach them that man does not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes from the mouth of the Lord—the background for the prayer for daily bread from God.
